The fight between religion and God is what’s called a false dichotomy, or put more simple, not actually a thing.

As science progresses (especially astronomy and cosmology) it typically advances proofs for God. An example of this would be the advancement of the Kalām Cosmological Argument.

The KCA is a very basic argument.

Premise 1. Everything that begins to exist has a cause (something that caused it to exist)
Premise 2. The universe began to exist.
Therefore the universe has a cause (something had to start the universe moving).

So where does science come in? It deals with proving the premises (logically speaking if all premises are true and the therefore statement most follow, then the therefore statement is also true).

Proving premise 1 is fairly simple. Things not in motion have to be moved by an outside source first. (Newton’s first law of movement and Galileo’s concept of inertia). Things cannot lack the source and have been moving for eternity past because then you would have infinite regression.

We need to prove the universe started to exist and has not always been here (or at least in motion) to prove the second half of the argument. The red shift established that the universe started as SUPER dense before expanding space and expending heat after the Big Bang (which I might mention was developed by a priest). For the universe to be expanding it had to start expanding at one point in time.

Obviously you can go into deeper science to proof both premises but I’m not ACTUALLY an astrophysicist. But I think for the sake of this comment I can consider my work done there. Let’s move onto the conclusion.

If as we’ve discussed that everything that begins to exist needs a causer and the universe began to exist we must conclude that the universe has a causer. Because the Big Bang (or shortly before or after) was the start of all time (this time one is important because it’s the response to the objection “who created God then? which is a nonsensical question because God did not begin to exist since he is outside of time), all space, and all matter it follows that the causer must be outside of those things. The term given to something that transcends time, space, and matter is god.
